note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ROK 4, 5, 10; A06b ROK 4, 5, 10; L05 ROK 15): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. General naturalisation costs ₩300,000 a person, paid in revenue stamps (Nationality Act art. 24, Enforcement Rule art. 18); the applicant sits the Social Integration Program's comprehensive evaluation, within a year of applying unless exempt, and an interview that examines Korean ability and the basic attitudes of a citizen (Enforcement Decree art. 4-2), as the Ministry of Government Legislation's Easylaw service states them. No longest time is published as a rule, so none is held.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, South Korea, 2024
sources.said: Person has been domiciled in South Korea for a continuous period of 5 years and has permanent residence status. ... Renunciation of citizenship of a foreign country (unless unreasonable to request). ... Person has voluntarily acquired citizenship of another country. Does not apply in the following cases if the person makes a declaration within 6 months of acquiring foreign citizenship to retain South Korean citizenship: person acquired the same citizenship as the spouse through marriage, the citizenship of an adoptive parent, the citizenship of another country after acknowledgment by a foreign father or mother, or the person is a minor child or spouse of a citizen who lost citizenship due to the acquisition of citizenship of another country. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in South Korea to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen. ... No provision ... No provision
